title: A 3D-$Δ$PDF-like measure for hidden anisotropy in disordered materials
authors: Helena Barker, Thomas C. Nicholas, Andrew L. Goodwin
abstract: We introduce a simple correlation function for quantifying hidden local anisotropy in disordered materials. Developed in analogy with the three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-$Δ$PDF), our approach identifies structural correlations that are lost through averaging over bulk symmetry. The same approach might be applied to models of disordered crystals, amorphous materials, and liquids alike.
summary: This paper introduces a novel measure, $\gamma_{ij}(r)$, to quantify hidden local structural anisotropy in disordered materials that is missed by standard pair distribution function analyses. By comparing local-coordinate correlations to bulk averages, the authors provide a diagnostic tool that reveals structural information related to local symmetry subgroups. This method is valuable for understanding the structural complexity in materials ranging from liquids to amorphous solids.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantify hidden local anisotropy in disordered materials, specifically identifying structural correlations that are lost when averaging over the bulk crystal symmetry.
main_result: A new measure, $\gamma_{ij}(r)$, is introduced which captures local structural correlations that are not accounted for by standard pair distribution functions, vanishing under the operation of the Laue group.
method: The method develops an analogy to the 3D-$\Delta$PDF, defining a local anisotropy measure $\gamma_{ij}(r)$ by comparing local-coordinate pair correlations ($	ilde{G}_{ij}(r)$) to global correlations ($\Delta G_{ij}(r)$).
model_or_system: The approach is applicable to various disordered systems, including amorphous materials, liquids (like water), and crystalline systems exhibiting local symmetry subgroups (e.g., $C_{2v}$ within $O_h$).
key_observables: The primary observable is $\gamma_{ij}(r) = \Delta	ilde{G}_{ij}(r) - \Delta G_{ij}(r)$, which quantifies the difference between local and average pairwise vector correlations.
important_parameters: The local coordinate system and the specific atomic model used to define the local correlations are crucial inputs.
main_assumptions: The local-coordinate variants depend entirely on the physicality of the atomistic model used, and $\gamma_{ij}(r)$ encodes higher-order correlations not uniquely determined by two-body scattering measurements.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept by defining the local anisotropy measure $\gamma_{ij}(r)$ in analogy to the 3D-$\Delta$PDF, derives its properties (e.g., vanishing under Laue group operations), and applies it to model systems to demonstrate its utility in revealing hidden local symmetries.
why_interesting: While focused on structural physics, the development of a new, symmetry-constrained correlation function ($\gamma_{ij}(r)$) represents a sophisticated theoretical diagnostic tool for analyzing complex, disordered many-body systems, which has parallels in analyzing entanglement structures in quantum many-body systems.
